label: Floer Homology
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 487 through 530 and turns Morse theory into infinite dimensions. We build a chain complex whose generators are periodic orbits of a Hamiltonian, whose differential counts cylinders, and whose homology recovers the homology of the manifold, settling the Arnold conjecture along the way.

label: The Symplectic Action Functional
notes: The action functional lives on the contractible loop space lifted with capping discs. Its critical points are exactly the one-periodic orbits of the Hamiltonian, so finding orbits becomes a variational problem. The action is unbounded above and below, which is why ordinary Morse theory fails and Floer's idea is needed.

label: Periodic Orbits as Critical Points
notes: Setting the first variation of the action to zero recovers Hamilton's equation, so critical loops are precisely the closed orbits. Nondegeneracy of an orbit means the linearized return map has no eigenvalue one, guaranteeing that orbits are isolated and that the generating set of the complex is finite.

label: Floer Cylinders: The Gradient Equation
notes: Negative gradient flow lines of the action with respect to the L-two metric are cylinders solving a perturbed Cauchy-Riemann equation. Finite energy forces each cylinder to converge at its two ends to periodic orbits, so the trajectories interpolate between critical points just like Morse flow lines connect critical points downhill.

label: The Conley-Zehnder Grading
notes: Each capped orbit carries a Conley-Zehnder index built from the path of symplectic matrices the linearized flow traces. This index grades the complex and equals the spectral flow of the linearized Floer operator, so the dimension of a cylinder moduli space is the difference of the two endpoint indices.

label: The Floer Chain Complex
notes: The chain groups are the free module on capped orbits over the Novikov ring, graded by the Conley-Zehnder index. The differential counts rigid index-one cylinders modulo the R translation action, weighting each by its energy. This packages all the orbit and cylinder data into one algebraic object.

label: Why d squared equals zero
notes: The square of the differential counts ends of one-dimensional moduli spaces of index-two cylinders. Compactness and gluing show these spaces compactify by adding exactly the broken trajectories, pairs of index-one cylinders. Since a compact one-manifold has an even boundary, every broken pair cancels and the square vanishes.

label: Invariance Under the Hamiltonian
notes: Different regular Hamiltonian and almost complex choices give different complexes, but continuation maps built from homotopies of the data induce chain homotopy equivalences. Hence Floer homology depends only on the manifold, not on the auxiliary choices, and becomes a genuine symplectic invariant of the closed manifold.

label: Isomorphism with Morse Homology
notes: For a small time-independent Hamiltonian the orbits are the critical points of a Morse function and the cylinders degenerate to Morse gradient lines. This identifies Floer homology with the Morse, hence singular, homology of the manifold, providing the bridge from dynamics to topology.

label: The Arnold Conjecture
notes: Counting generators bounds homology from below, so the number of nondegenerate one-periodic orbits is at least the total Betti number. This vastly improves the classical Lefschetz fixed point estimate, which only gives the Euler characteristic, and resolves the homological Arnold conjecture for closed symplectic manifolds.

label: The Pair-of-Pants Product
notes: Counting solutions over a three-punctured sphere defines a product on Floer homology. This pair-of-pants count is associative and unital and, transported through PSS, becomes the quantum cup product, deforming the classical cup product by counting rational curves weighted by Novikov variables.

label: PSS and Quantum Cohomology
notes: The Piunikhin-Salamon-Schwarz maps cap orbits with half-cylinders carrying spiked discs, giving a ring isomorphism between Floer homology and quantum cohomology. Through PSS the pair-of-pants product matches the quantum product, completing the dictionary between Hamiltonian dynamics and enumerative quantum geometry.
